name: Industrial IoT and predictive maintenance
summary: Connected equipment streams operating data so organizations can detect degradation, schedule maintenance and improve performance.
useCase: A sensor system identifies an unusual vibration pattern in a pump, creates a maintenance recommendation and checks whether the intervention prevented failure.
whyNow: Sensors, connectivity and analytics are established, while applying them consistently across heterogeneous industrial assets remains uneven. IoT Analytics estimated 21.1 billion connected IoT devices at the end of 2025 and described a shift toward autonomous connected operations. That broad device count includes many nonindustrial products. The valuable emerging layer is dependable operational insight and action, rather than connecting equipment without a business result.

mainstream.scope: Condition monitoring and predictive maintenance used routinely for economically important assets in medium and large industrial organizations.
mainstream.rationale: The enabling stack is mature and downtime provides a measurable business case. Adoption should expand through existing controls, maintenance and equipment suppliers. The date assumes integration with maintenance processes and trustworthy failure labels. Rare failures, small sites and legacy machinery can keep some applications uneconomic.

metric.name: Connected IoT devices worldwide — adjacent infrastructure proxy
metric.scope: IoT Analytics estimates for all IoT, including industrial and nonindustrial devices.
metric.growthLabel: Estimated installed base grew about 14% in 2025
metric.limitations: Research estimates rather than a device census. The 2024 value is a revised estimate, not the earlier 18.8 billion forecast. The denominator includes consumer and nonindustrial IoT, so this is an enabling-infrastructure proxy, not predictive-maintenance adoption.
metric.futureNote: IoT Analytics’ forecast concerns total connected IoT devices. It does not imply the same growth rate for industrial analytics revenue, autonomous operations or predictive maintenance.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No retrospectively harmonized annual device value is inserted; older estimates used different revisions.
No comparable industrial predictive-maintenance adoption census identified.
No stable industry-wide maintenance-analytics penetration figure supplied.
IoT Analytics’ later revised estimate placed the connected IoT base at 18.5 billion.
The year-end IoT base was estimated at 21.1 billion; the broad enterprise ecosystem continued expanding.
IoT Analytics described more autonomous connected operations; PTC completed the sale of ThingWorx and Kepware to TPG.

tailwinds: Avoided downtime, reduced scrap and better energy performance create measurable value.
Existing installed sensors and maintenance systems provide a route to expand useful analytics.
bottlenecks: Inconsistent asset data, missing failure labels and difficult legacy integration reduce model reliability.
A useful alert must trigger an effective maintenance process; false alarms can destroy trust.
watchMetrics: Unplanned downtime and maintenance cost per operating hour, with control groups where feasible.
Precision of actionable failure alerts, avoided failures and expansion to additional paying assets.
